entries.title: II Corinthians 3:1
segments: ¶Do we begin again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, as some [others], epistles of commendation to you or [letters] of commendation from you?

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:2
segments: You are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read by all men;

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:3
segments: clearly [you are] an epistle of Christ, ministered by us, written not with ink but by the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of flesh, [that is], of the heart.

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:4
segments: And we have such trust through Christ toward God.

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:5
segments: Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think of anything as [being] from ourselves, but our sufficiency [is] from God,

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:6
segments: ¶who also made us sufficient as ministers of the new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:7
segments: But if the ministry of death, written [and] engraved on stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not look steadily at the face of Moses because of the glory of his countenance, which [glory] was passing away,

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:8
segments: how will the ministry of the Spirit not be more glorious?

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:9
segments: For if the ministry of condemnation [had] glory, the ministry of righteousness exceeds much more in glory.

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:10
segments: For even what was made glorious had no glory in this respect, because of the glory that excels.

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:11
segments: For if what is passing away [was] glorious, what remains [is] much more glorious.

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:12
segments: ¶Therefore, since we have such hope, we use great boldness of speech--

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:13
segments: unlike Moses, [who] put a veil over his face so that the children of Israel could not look steadily at the end of what was passing away.

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:14
segments: But their minds were blinded. For until this day the same veil remains unlifted in the reading of the Old Testament, because the [veil] is taken away in Christ.

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:15
segments: But even to this day, when Moses is read, a veil lies on their heart.

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:16
segments: Nevertheless when one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:17
segments: Now the Lord is the Spirit; and where the Spirit of the Lord [is], there [is] liberty.

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:18
segments: But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as by the Spirit of the Lord.
